description: The bar chart visually compares the CoLeG-R (%) performance across three LLaMA-2 model sizes — 7B, 13B, and 70B — under four distinct fine-tuning conditions, with each condition represented by a uniquely patterned and colored bar within each model group. The horizontal axis lists the model sizes in ascending parameter order, while the vertical axis, labeled “CoLeG-R (%)”, spans from 0 to 80 with linear increments of 10. For each model, the four bars — from left to right — correspond to: “no SFT” (light blue with diagonal white stripes), “+ SFT on D₀” (yellow with horizontal white stripes), “+ SFT on D₀, D₁” (light purple with slanted stripes), and “+ SFT on D₀, D₁, D₂” (peach solid fill), as indicated by the legend in the bottom-right corner. In the 7B model, performance increases from ~66% (no SFT) to ~78% (full SFT), showing consistent gains with additional data. The 13B model starts at ~70%, rises to ~72% with D₀, peaks at ~78% with D₀+D₁, then slightly drops to ~76% with D₂. The 70B model begins at just over 80%, climbs to 81% with D₀, then declines to ~78% with D₀+D₁ and further to ~76% with full SFT, suggesting that for the largest model, additional fine-tuning data beyond D₀ yields diminishing or even negative returns. The bars are not sorted by height within each group, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond their color and pattern coding. The chart’s structure and data trends support the paper’s observation that scaling SFT data improves smaller models but offers limited or declining benefits for larger ones.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates the CoLeG-R (%) performances for different models under varying conditions. The horizontal axis contains the categories labeled as 'LLAMA-2-7B', 'LLAMA-2-13B', and 'LLAMA-2-70B'. The vertical axis represents the CoLeG-R percentage, labeled as 'CoLeG-R (%)' with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 80, and numerical tick marks at intervals of 10. Each category consists of four stacked bars representing different conditions: 'no SFT' in blue with white diagonal stripes, '+ SFT on D₀' in yellow with white horizontal stripes patterns, '+ SFT on D₀, D₁' in purple with slanted stripes, and '+ SFT on D₀, D₁, D₂' in peach with solid fill. For LLAMA-2-7B, the blue bar reaches approximately 66%, yellow at 66%, purple at around 75%, and red close to 78%. For LLAMA-2-13B, the blue bar is around 70%, yellow at 72%, purple at approximately 78%, and red about 76%. For LLAMA-2-70B, the blue bar is just above 80%, yellow at 81%, purple around 78%, and red reaching close to 76%. The results suggest that scaling up the SFT dataset leads to diminishing returns for larger models, as the performance of LLAMA-2-70B stabilizes across conditions. A legend is given bottom right.
